title: Utilization signal playbook for dynamic slices
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for using short-timescale utilization signals to drive dynamic slice sizing and soft pricing bands for the Dedicated product. Goal is to reduce wasted reserved GPU hours while preserving predictable latency/throughput for SLA customers.

High-level idea (one-liner):
- Use simple, robust utilization signals and a small set of control levers (slice target utilization, smoothing horizon, min capacity floor, backfill budget) to dynamically reallocate reserved pool capacity across latency-sensitive and throughput-oriented slices and to trigger priced burst or preemptable routing.

Terms / quick glossary:
- slice: a named sub-pool carved from a reserved GPU pool (e.g. fast-lane, bulk, backfill).
- signal window: the lookback period for utilization (minutes/hours).
- target_util: the desired long-run utilization for a slice (e.g., 65%).
- cushion: extra headroom reserved to absorb bursts (expressed in GPU-hours).
- backfill budget: percent of idle capacity allowed to be sold as spot/backfill.

Core signals we recommend (robust and cheap to compute):
1) instantaneous_util = busy_gpus / total_allocated_gpus (sampled every 30s)
2) ema_util(t) = EMA(instantaneous_util, alpha) with alpha corresponding to a 15–60 minute effective window (alpha ~ 0.01–0.05 depending on cadence)
3) tail_95_latency(ms) per route (used as safety veto for shrink actions)
4) time_since_last_scale_up (minutes) to enforce cool-downs

Control knobs (user-facing and internal):
- slice_target_util (per-slice setting)
- min_slice_capacity (absolute GPUs pinned)
- cushion_hours (per-slice soft buffer)
- backfill_pct (how much idle capacity can be re-sold)
- burst_price_multiplier (multiplier applied when routing to burst/shared infra)

Operational heuristics (recommendations):
- Only shrink a slice if ema_util < target_util - hysteresis_band (hysteresis_band = 7–12%) AND tail_95_latency within SLO for 30m window.
- Only grow a slice if ema_util > target_util + hysteresis_band OR instantaneous_util > 90% for sustained 3m and queuing observed.
- Enforce min_slice_capacity so very small customers do not oscillate and to maintain minimum GPU granularity.
- Use a time-based exponential penalty for repeated scale-downs to avoid oscillation (e.g., disallow shrink for 60m after a shrink).

Pricing bands and soft routing policy (sketch):
- baseline: customer runs inside their slice at committed rate (monthly/annual commit pricing).
- soft-burst: when project exceeds allocated slice, route to dedicated-burst pool with price_multiplier = 1.6x baseline (temporary, no SLA).
- preemptable-backfill: use preemptable instances at price_multiplier = 0.45x baseline when backfill budget allows. These are throttled and can be reclaimed.
- graceful-fallback: if both burst and preemptable exhausted, route to hosted API fallback (higher latency) at price_multiplier = 2.0x with priority-based token throttling.

Spreadsheet layout suggestions (columns to include in model sheet):
- slice_name, date, hour_start, allocated_gpus, busy_gpu_seconds, idle_gpu_seconds, instantaneous_util, ema_util, tail_95_latency_ms, scale_action, action_reason, post_allocated_gpus, cushion_hours_remaining, backfill_used_pct, billed_gpu_hours, effective_unit_cost

Example row (CSV snippet):
slice_name,hour_start,allocated_gpus,busy_gpu_seconds,idle_gpu_seconds,instantaneous_util,ema_util,tail_95_latency_ms,scale_action,post_allocated_gpus,billed_gpu_hours,effective_unit_cost
fast-lane,2026-02-09T13:00Z,8,25000,3500,0.877,0.82,48,grow,10,9.6,$6.25
bulk,2026-02-09T13:00Z,24,65000,22000,0.747,0.70,102,none,24,24,$2.10

Key formulas (plain text, place as comments/notes in sheet):
- instantaneous_util = busy_gpu_seconds / (allocated_gpus * 3600)  # per hour aggregation
- ema_util_t = alpha * instantaneous_util_t + (1 - alpha) * ema_util_{t-1}
- billed_gpu_hours = max(allocated_gpus, post_allocated_gpus) * 1 hour adjusted for cushion sellable time
- effective_unit_cost = committed_monthly_cost / (utilization_factor * total_available_hours_in_month) -> sanity check with observed billed hours

Backfill and accounting rules (operational):
- Only count backfill hours as billable to spot customers. Committed customers see usage beyond cushion charged at burst_rate.
- Keep a rolling 7-day backfill ledger per pool to ensure backfill_used_pct <= backfill_pct.
- When preemptions exceed X% of backfill used for customer Y, reduce their backfill allocation next window.

Risk & safety vetoes:
- Never shrink if any route has tail_99_latency > SLA_threshold over 10m window.
- Protect customers with explicit "no-burst" flag (they cannot be forced onto burst infra).
- Always prefer preemptable for non-latency-critical batch shards; prefer burst for low-latency but small overrun.

Simulation notes (how to test in spreadsheet):
- Use historic per-minute sampled data for a representative 30d window. Aggregate to hour buckets for quick experiments.
- Run three scenarios: conservative (low alpha, wide hysteresis, backfill_pct=20%), aggressive (high alpha, narrow hysteresis, backfill_pct=45%), baseline (current defaults). Compare idle-hours, billed-hours, customer_impact events (scale_count, forced_burst_count).
- Key KPIs: pool_util_avg, pool_util_p95, idle_gpu_hours_saved, customer_slo_breach_events, billed_revenue_delta, marginal_cost_per_gpu_hr.

Example small sensitivity table to paste into sheet (CSV):
param,conservative,baseline,aggressive
ema_alpha,0.01,0.03,0.08
hysteresis_pct,12,8,5
backfill_pct,20,30,45
burst_multiplier,1.4,1.6,1.8

Operational checklist (for rollout):
- [ ] Implement ema_util and instantaneous sampling in metrics pipeline (SRE/infra).
- [ ] Add slice metadata fields to console (min_capacity, target_util, no_burst flag).
- [ ] Wire up experiment mode for dynamic slice actions: start in read-only (alerts only) -> shadow reallocation -> automated with 1% of pools -> ramp.
- [ ] Build billing mapping: ensure burst/preemptable hours are tagged in billing exports.
- [ ] Run 30d simulation on historical traces and present results to PM + SRE.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: How do we map cushion_hours to per-customer SLAs in contracts? (legal/pricing input needed)
- Q: Should backfill be sold only to spot customers or to commercial customers who opt-in? Tradeoff: revenue vs predictability.
- TODO: run a 7-day sensitivity with synthetic burst events (10–20x request rate) to validate hysteresis and cool-down config.
- TODO: produce a one-pager for sales teams explaining soft-burst vs preemptable difference.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the spreadsheet simple at first. Avoid overfitting knobs. The 3-parameter family (alpha, hysteresis, backfill_pct) buys most of the benefit.
- If we observe oscillation in simulation, add a simple backoff multiplier to shrink amplitude instead of introducing more state.

References and related docs:
- see product/dedicated/gpu-pool-slab-pricing-idle-sink-analysis (internal reference, earlier work)
- see backlog ticket JIRA-RDW-9876 for billing tagging details

Next steps (short):
1) Get infra to emit 30s instantaneous_util + tail percentiles by route (SRE).
2) Build sample sheet with two pools (us-west-2a, eu-west-1b) and run baseline vs aggressive.
3) Demo results to product leadership and pick defaults for alpha/hysteresis/backfill_pct.

-- end of draft playbook. This is intentionally rough; meant to be pasted into a Drive doc and iterated in real time.
